name_note: One genome GTDB places in this species is deposited at NCBI under the name Actinomyces viscosus.

sentences.text: Actinomyces oris is described as a key oral commensal involved in dental plaque formation, and the genome of strain MG-1 is a single circular chromosome of 3,042,829 base pairs.
It is reported to play an important role in oral biofilm development and, like many Gram-positive bacteria, to anchor many surface proteins to peptidoglycan through the housekeeping sortase SrtA.
The species expresses type 1 and type 2 fimbriae on its surface, with type 2 fimbriae reported to mediate co-aggregation and biofilm formation.
That report states that endocarditis caused by Actinomyces is extremely rare, with one prior case of Actinomyces oris endocarditis reported before theirs.
